summary.summary: April 16 is a convergence day of negative catalysts. Nvidia disclosed a $5.5B charge from H20 China export ban (announced after close April 15). ASML reported weak bookings (EUR 3.94B vs EUR 4.89B expected). AMD followed with $800M charge from export controls. Powell speaks at 1:30 PM ET at Economic Club of Chicago — will warn about tariff-driven inflation and growth tension, creating 'challenging scenario' for dual mandate. Retail sales data (8:30 AM) showed strong March numbers (+1.4%) but this is backward-looking pre-tariff data reflecting consumers front-running price increases. Gold broke $3,300 for first time. Dollar at 3-year lows. The semiconductor sector is under severe pressure from export controls, and Powell's afternoon speech creates a catalyst for further afternoon selling.

actualOutcome.narrative: Stocks sold off hard. Semiconductors led decline (NVDA -6.9%, AMD -7%, ASML -5%). Powell's 1:30 PM speech at Economic Club of Chicago warned of stagflation risk from tariffs, pushing stocks to session lows in the afternoon. Gold surged past $3,300 to record highs. Broad risk-off session.

scenarios.trade: Nvidia is the epicenter of the April 16 sell-off. The $5.5B H20 charge is a clear negative catalyst with no ambiguity. The H20 was specifically designed to comply with prior export rules — this ban closes the last legal pathway for AI chip sales to China, a $12-15B annual revenue pool. Semiconductor peers (AMD, ASML) also reporting bad news, creating sector-wide contagion. Powell's afternoon speech will add macro selling pressure. The structural message is the real damage: no chip design can safely target China.

scenarios.implication: Some of the H20 charge may already be priced into pre-market. Dip buyers could emerge around $100-105 technical support. If Powell is less hawkish than expected, afternoon could see a bounce. Long-term AI capex narrative still intact for domestic customers.

scenarios.trade: The VanEck Semiconductor ETF provides broad semiconductor short exposure on a day when the entire sector is under coordinated assault from different but related catalysts. This is not a single-stock event; it's a sector-wide re-rating of China revenue exposure. SMH avoids single-stock risk while capturing the sector theme. The export control escalation represents a paradigm shift — chips designed for compliance are no longer safe. Powell speech at 1:30 PM adds another selling catalyst mid-session.

scenarios.implication: ETF has broad diversification including names less exposed to China (TXN, some AVGO domestic revenue). Electronics tariff exemption from April 11 provides some buffer. Sector may find support at key technical levels. Dip buyers historically active in semis.

scenarios.trade: SPDR Gold Trust is the cleanest way to play the gold breakout above $3,300 without mining stock equity correlation risk. On a day when equities sell off hard, gold decouples and surges. Powell's 1:30 PM speech explicitly flagging stagflation risks will be an additional catalyst for gold inflows. Dollar weakness, record ETF inflows, and central bank buying provide structural support. Unlike gold miners, GLD won't get dragged down by equity market correlation.

scenarios.implication: Gold could be over-extended after 26% YTD rally. Profit-taking possible at round-number resistance ($3,350, $3,400). If retail sales data is interpreted as 'economy still strong,' some safe-haven bid may dissipate temporarily. Spreads can widen in volatile sessions.

scenarios.trade: Newmont is the premier gold mining play on a day when gold breaks $3,300 for the first time in history. Gold miners have 2-3x operating leverage to the gold price — if gold is up 3%, NEM could move 6-9%. The macro setup is perfect: dollar at 3-year lows, trade war escalating, Powell about to warn of stagflation, VIX elevated. Gold ETF inflows hit $21.1B in Q1. Newmont's cost structure means ~80% of incremental gold price flows to bottom line above $2,500/oz. Central bank gold buying provides structural floor.

scenarios.implication: Gold miners often lag the metal on volatile days due to equity market correlation. If broad market selloff is severe enough, NEM could get dragged down with equities despite gold strength. Mining operational risks independent of gold price. Profit-taking possible after strong YTD run.

scenarios.trade: Bookings are the leading indicator for ASML — they signal future revenue 12-18 months out. A 20% miss is material. The company widened Q2 gross margin guidance band explicitly citing tariff uncertainty. If Nvidia and AMD are cutting China orders due to export controls, ASML's EUV tool demand is directly impacted. The consensus estimate was already cautious — missing it badly is a negative signal. Powell's afternoon speech adds macro pressure.

scenarios.implication: Revenue was in-line and gross margin beat at 54%. Full-year guidance maintained (EUR 30-35B). High-NA system momentum continues with 5th system shipped. Monopoly position in EUV provides structural support. Some bookings weakness may be timing-related.

scenarios.trade: In a risk-off environment, money flows from high-beta tech into defensive sectors. TRV is a Dow component with zero China exposure, strong pricing power in insurance hardening market, and a verified earnings beat. The underlying combined ratio improvement of 2.9 points signals fundamental strength. Net investment income up 10%. California wildfire losses are a known one-time event. This is a relative-value long on a risk-off day.

scenarios.implication: Broader market selloff could drag even strong earners lower — correlation spikes in panic selling. $2.27B wildfire losses are significant and could recur. If Powell triggers severe risk-off, even defensive names may sell. Dow component means it contributes to index-level selling pressure.
